disclaimer: All revenue, funding, debt, GPU-count, contract and risk figures are compiled from public company announcements, SEC/press filings and press reporting. They are best-effort estimates for visualization and education, NOT investment advice or authoritative financial data. Figures move fast in this sector -- verify against primary sources (10-K/6-K filings, company IR pages) before relying on them. Site coordinates are metro/campus-level approximations.

risk_methodology.name: Neocloud Risk Score

factor_definitions.customer_concentration: Share of revenue/backlog tied to one or two anchor customers. A single customer walking away (or renegotiating) can gut the business.
factor_definitions.leverage: Reliance on debt / SPV / vendor-financing structures (incl. circular vendor financing where a chip supplier is simultaneously investor, lender and customer) rather than equity to fund GPU and data-center capex.
factor_definitions.contract_mismatch: Gap between the tenor of debt/financing backing the GPUs and the tenor of the revenue contracts covering them. Short contracts stacked on long-dated debt = refinancing risk; long contracts that lock in one chip generation = obsolescence lock-in risk. For pure data-center landlords (no GPU ownership), this instead reflects lease structure -- long triple-net-style leases transfer the GPU refresh risk entirely to the GPU-owning tenant.
factor_definitions.chip_freshness: How exposed the fleet is to obsolescence. Majority-Hopper (H100/H200) or older AMD fleets score higher risk than fleets already on Blackwell/GB200-300/MI350-class silicon -- the crux of the Burry-style 'GPUs depreciate over 2-3 years, not 5-6' debate.

risk_methodology.note: Landlord-model companies (own the building/power, not the GPUs) are scored on the same rubric for comparability, but their chip_freshness factor is neutral (40) since they carry no direct chip-obsolescence exposure -- their risk is almost entirely tenant-concentration risk, which the score is designed to surface.

companies.name: CoreWeave
companies.gpu_owner_detail: CoreWeave buys and owns the GPUs, financed largely with GPU-collateralized debt (SPVs backed by Magnetar, Blackstone, and others) rather than equity.
companies.revenue_note: FY2025 revenue $5.13B, +170% YoY from $1.92B in 2024. FY2026 guidance $12-13B.
companies.debt_note: $21.6B total indebtedness disclosed in FY2025 10-K, plus a further $8.5B delayed-draw term loan (Mar 2026) tied to a single customer contract.
companies.risk_notes: Aggressively diversifying away from Microsoft (OpenAI, Meta, Nvidia deals) but still carries the heaviest disclosed debt load ($21.6B+) of any neocloud, funded via GPU-collateralized SPVs.

companies.name: Lambda
companies.gpu_owner_detail: Owns most of its fleet, but in Sep 2025 Nvidia signed a $1.5B deal to lease back 18,000 GPUs from Lambda over 4 years -- a circular financing structure (supplier as tenant).
companies.revenue_note: Annualized run-rate ~$500M as of May 2025 (up from $425M run-rate Dec 2024); cloud GPU rental grew ~100% YoY in H1 2025.
companies.debt_note: Primarily equity-funded to date ($480M Series D Feb 2025 @ ~$4B val.; $1.5B Series E Nov 2025); Nvidia GPU lease-back adds a debt-like off-balance-sheet obligation.

companies.risk_notes: Diversified customer base with a fast-growing Microsoft/Nvidia anchor; among the first to production-scale GB300 NVL72, so obsolescence risk is comparatively low.

companies.name: TensorWave
companies.gpu_owner_detail: Owns its AMD Instinct fleet; AMD Ventures and Magnetar are both investors in and (via MI-series purchase commitments) beneficiaries of TensorWave's scale-up -- a circular financing pattern similar to Nvidia's with its neoclouds.
companies.revenue_note: Revenue run-rate grew from ~$5M (2024) to >$100M exiting 2025, a ~20x YoY increase.

customers.name: Diversified AI/enterprise workloads
customers.note: No single disclosed anchor customer at hyperscaler scale; growth pitch is AMD-alternative pricing/availability.

companies.risk_notes: Secured 2GW+ of long-term data-center capacity ahead of confirmed contracted demand of that scale -- a buildout-ahead-of-revenue pattern common across the sector's smaller challengers.

financing_graph.note: Directed edges src -> dst. This is the 'circular financing' web the sector is debated over: chip vendors invest in the neoclouds that buy their chips and in some cases lease compute back, while private credit funds the GPU purchases against the same GPUs as collateral.
